reject: the person or thing that is rejected or set aside as inferior in quality

I disapprove of her child rearing methods

dismiss from consideration or a contest
John was ruled out as a possible suspect because he had a strong alibi
This possibility can be eliminated from our consideration
rejection: his proposals were met with rejection

rejoicing: the utterance of sounds expressing great joy
joyful and proud especially because of triumph or success
rejoicing crowds filled the streets on VJ Day
rejoinder: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
it brought a sharp rejoinder from the teacher
(law) a pleading made by a defendant in response to the plaintiff's replication

the annual rejuvenation of the landscape
the act of restoring to a more youthful condition

rejective: rejective or overcritical attitudes of disappointed parents
